The form of the cosmological argument we’ll be discussing today is due to Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz. Leibniz was a German philosopher, mathematician, theologian, and scientist, whose achievements included the invention of calculus.
His intellect and achievements were such that they led Diderot, a later French philosopher, to remark that
“When one compares the talents one has with those of a Leibniz, one is tempted to throw away one's books and go die quietly in the dark of some forgotten corner.”
